closed_finding.fact: pi_uv_event_queue asserts !event->in_use and sets it; v2 only cleared event_queued, so a second completion would assert.
closed_finding.correction: v3 clears event->in_use only after actual FS FIFO removal under event_mutex, immediately before the release store to event_queued. Reset and older event release still do not mutate next/in_use.

conclusions: The new queued release store precedes completed release; an acquire observation of completion therefore cannot admit Reset during the completion-before-enqueue window.
Actual dequeue removes the embedded node/next link and clears the FS slot admission state before exposing the event; Reset still requires completed and actual cleaned, not merely an old host ticket.

Original synchronous command admission serializes reset/resubmit with worker access. The previous callback retains its request entitlement through final accesses; a later command cannot execute on the same worker until it returns.

Each accepted native completion retains a request and event_queue retains the service. The old ticket release snapshots only stable fields and drops one independent reference pair. It never clears the newly queued next link, in_use or event_queued.
A final request release can invoke cleanup only when no new native callback/queued ticket still owns the request. New in-flight and queued operations independently prevent that final release.

Raw span admission copies the caller's actual buffer fields, validates Windows ULONG extent, and retains no JS value or invented lease. The caller keeps the native storage through completion/cleanup, with stop/join before destruction.

Initial Reset is a no-op only for unsubmitted uncleaned storage. Completed native rejection has no queued event and may reset only after real cleanup. After service stop, resubmission returns actual unaccepted cancellation and queues nothing.

Assigned controls distinguish ticket entitlement from event address; they test uncleaned/queued rejection, repeat ownership, FIFO A-before-B after old release, and final request lifetime after explicit owner plus old ticket retirement. Every acquired event enters the fixture before fallible assertions; teardown joins before borrowed spans/descriptors retire.
